1. (Currently Amended) A cell comprising: a non-native compartment comprising a proteinaceous shell comprising at least one bacterial microcompartment (BMC) polypeptide, wherein the non-native compartment is formed by self-assembly of the proteinaceous shell in a host cell.

2. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 wherein the non-native compartment further comprises at least one targeted enzyme that occupies a defined spatial arrangement within the compartment.

3. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 wherein the non-native compartment further comprises at least one targeted enzyme that catalyzes a specific metabolic reaction within the compartment.

4. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 3 wherein the non-native compartment comprises a plurality of different targeted enzymes that are selected based on their metabolic activity.

5. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 3 wherein the at least one targeted enzyme comprises a compartment-specific targeting signal sequence that directs its localization within the non-native compartment.

6. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 wherein the BMC polypeptide comprises an Eut polypeptide that enhances the compartment's biochemical capabilities.

7. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 6 wherein the Eut polypeptide comprises an EutS polypeptide that is involved in the compartment's metabolic functions.

8. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 wherein the proteinaceous shell comprises a plurality of different BMC polypeptides that each contribute to the integrity and functionality of the shell.

9. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 8 wherein the plurality of different BMC polypeptides comprises BMC polypeptides from at least two different bacterial species that provide diverse metabolic functions.

10. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 8 wherein the plurality of different BMC polypeptides comprises BMC polypeptides from at least two different BMC operons that confer specialized functions to the compartment.

11. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 wherein at least one BMC polypeptide comprises an affinity tag that enables selective isolation of the non-native compartment from a biological mixture.

12. (Currently Amended) A method comprising: introducing into a host cell a polynucleotide that encodes at least one BMC polypeptide and an enzyme that catalyzes a specific reaction, thereby producing a transformed cell; and growing the transformed cell under conditions effective for the transformed cell to express the polynucleotide that encodes at least one BMC polypeptide and produce a non-native compartment comprising a proteinaceous shell comprising the at least one BMC polypeptide and the at least one enzyme.

13. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 12 wherein the host cell comprises a bacterium engineered to express a modified metabolic pathway.

14. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 13 wherein the bacterium comprises a member of the family Enterobacteriaceae that enhances enzyme activity within the compartment.

15. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 14 wherein the member of the family Enterobacteriaceae comprises E. coli treated to improve BMC assembly and enzyme function.

16. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 13 wherein the bacterium comprises a member of the family Shewanellaceae that supports environmental adaptability.

17. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 12 wherein the host cell comprises a yeast that has been modified for optimal enzyme activity.

18. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 17 wherein the yeast comprises a member of the family Saccharomycetaceae utilized for metabolic engineering.

19. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 18 wherein the member of the family Saccharomycetaceae comprises Saccharomyces cerevisiae engineered for product formation.

20. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 12 wherein the host cell comprises an alga modified to enhance biofuel production.

21. (Currently Amended) A method comprising: providing a cell comprising a non-native compartment comprising: a proteinaceous shell comprising at least one bacterial microcompartment (BMC) polypeptide, and at least one enzyme that catalyzes conversion of a substrate to a product in situ; and growing the cell under conditions effective for the at least one enzyme to catalyze conversion of the substrate to a product.

22. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 21 wherein the product comprises a biologically active product derived from a microbial metabolic pathway.

23. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 21 wherein the product comprises a drug or a precursor that is derived from the enzymatic reaction occurring within the compartment.

24. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 21 wherein the product comprises a biofuel or a precursor of biofuel production from renewable sources.

25. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 21 wherein the at least one enzyme catalyzes a step in degrading or detoxifying a toxic substrate to render it non-toxic.

26. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 21 further comprising isolating at least a portion of the non-native compartments from the growth medium.

27. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 26 wherein at least a portion of the non-native compartment comprises an affinity tag and isolating at least a portion of the non-native compartments comprises contacting a sample comprising the non-native compartments with an affinity substrate having selective affinity for the affinity tag.

28. (Currently Amended) The cell of claim 1 comprising a plurality of compartments wherein the compartments exhibit distinct biochemical activities relevant to metabolic pathways.
